one_line_contribution: A pre-registered dose ladder (k_train in {0,1,3,7} plus a length-matched relevance-destroyed decoy) that tests whether the information-abundance effect — relevant training-time context suppressing parametric encoding, with an intermediate optimum and rising context-fragility — holds for agent trajectories rather than documents, and whether the per-type context-explained action-token loss at initialization predicts where the deficit lands.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2608.12218 (Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge, 2026-08-12) — VERIFIED twice this session, once by `s2cli paper` (s2 channel) and once as the top hit of my recent-restricted mechanism query (hf channel). Its one-line finding is 'longer training contexts can reduce parametric knowledge encoding and increase contextual reliance, causing performance to decline beyond an intermediate optimum.' That is P1 (non-monotone retention with an intermediate optimum) and P3 (rising context reliance/fragility) already, and the proposal concedes it is the mechanism source. What survives is a domain port (agent trajectories/ALFWorld instead of documents/generic SFT), the relevance-destroyed decoy control, the distillation-side arm, and the dl-signature. That is an incremental novelty budget, and it is not helped by the QA-side literature my searches surfaced: arXiv:2410.05983 (Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG, hf) already studies how performance degrades as the number of retrieved passages grows and proposes training-based fixes, and arXiv:2310.01558 (Making Retrieval-Augmented LMs Robust to Irrelevant Context, hf) already fine-tunes on a *mixture* of relevant and irrelevant contexts to change inference-time reliance — i.e. the dose axis and the decoy-style control both exist outside agents. Second threat: arXiv:2603.18272 (Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience, VERIFIED via s2cli paper, s2, 'retrieval-aware fine-tuning' on agents, 5 citations) is the proposal's own closest named method; I could verify its existence and framing but NOT its ablation section (WebSearch unavailable), so the proposal's assertion that it 'never varies the dose' is unverified — a k-ablation is the single most standard ablation such a paper would run, and if it exists the ladder is a re-run. Third, weaker but on the mechanism: arXiv:2606.01967 (Training Prompt Matters: State-Adaptive Optimization for Robust Fine-Tuning, hf, abstract only) reports that training prompts shape learning dynamics and that superior prompts are identifiable through task-loss analysis, which is the dl-signature idea in a non-agent setting; and arXiv:2606.04703 (Rethinking Continual Experience Internalization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents, hf, abstract only) reports findings on 'experience granularity, injection patterns, and internalization regimes' for agents — 'injection patterns' may or may not be a dose manipulation, and neither the proposal nor I verified it.
strongest_objection: The headline is a domain replication of a three-week-old verified result, and the one genuinely new component — the context-explained-loss signature — is tested by a correlation that cannot come out negative if the dose effect exists at all. P4 correlates D_t(k) (the encoding deficit) against dl_t(k) (context-explained loss) across (type, dose) cells. Both quantities are monotone in k by construction: dl grows with k because more retrieved items explain more of the action-token NLL, and D grows with k under the hypothesis. So a pooled rho >= 0.5 across cells is delivered by the shared dose axis alone, with no per-type mechanism required; a model in which the dose effect is a uniform long-prefix optimization artefact spread evenly over types would produce the same rho. The only test that separates the mechanism from the dose axis is the *within-dose, across-type* correlation (or a partial correlation with k residualized out), and that is exactly the analysis whose per-type cells the proposal itself concedes carry +/-13-15 point floors — on six ALFWorld types that is roughly n=6 per dose with error bars wider than the spread. Compounding it: the confirmatory contrasts are pre-registered at 0.15 g ~ 4-5 net points against a stated pooled CI of +/-4.6, so P1 and P6 sit at or below the noise floor before any multiplicity correction across 4 doses x 3 conditions x 2 pools; P6's requirement of non-overlapping bootstrap argmax sets over a 4-rung ladder at that precision is close to unachievable, so the routing claim — the part the abstract sells — is likely to return 'inconclusive' rather than either 'confirmed' or 'falsified'.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the mechanism test non-circular: pre-register the within-dose across-type correlation (or partial rho with k residualized), and add a manipulation rather than an observation — e.g. re-rank retrieval to build a *high-dl k=1* condition and a *low-dl k=7* condition, so dl and token count are crossed instead of collinear. If low-dl k=7 shows no deficit and high-dl k=1 does, the loss-explained account is established; a correlation across a collinear ladder never will be. (2) Fix the cross-pool prediction: the self-rollout pool is the base model's own k=0 successes, i.e. the tasks with low dl by selection, so 'smaller dl and a smaller dose effect on the self-rollout pool' is entailed by how the pool was built and violates the brief's no-definitional-prediction rule. Match task-type composition across pools (subsample the expert pool to the same task instances the self-rollout pool covers) before comparing dose effects. (3) Fix the positive control: pick-and-place has dl ~ 0 *and* is already near ceiling at k=0, so 'no dose effect there' is equally explained by ceiling; find or construct a low-dl type that is not at ceiling, or report the control on the NLL proxy where ceiling does not apply. (4) Buy power where the claim lives: drop the k=1 rung and the CD k_s=3 arm and spend the episodes on seeds for k in {0,3,7} in the three test conditions, or state P1/P6 on the deterministic memory-free NLL proxy as primary with episodes as confirmation. (5) Verify 2603.18272's ablations before claiming the dose ladder is new.
missing_baseline: A relevance-destroyed, token-matched decoy at k=7 (decoy-7). The decoy exists only at k=3, but the load-bearing half of P1 is the *drop* at k=7 — r(7) < r(0) by >= 0.15 g. With a placebo only at the dose where no drop is predicted, 'r(7) < r(0)' remains fully explained by 'a ~1,010-token irrelevant prefix hurts step-level QLoRA', which is precisely the confound the decoy arm was introduced to kill and precisely the binding objection that sank memory_in_the_loop_training_decomposition in round 2. A second omission in the same family: no arm equalizes optimization scale across doses — as k_train rises, the action-token loss falls because the context explains it, so the k=7 arm receives systematically smaller gradients per example; logging gradient norms is diagnosis, not control. A loss-rescaled (or gradient-norm-matched) k=7 arm separates 'relevant context reduces the pressure to encode' from 'the arm simply took fewer effective updates', and without it the mechanism and a mundane effective-learning-rate story make identical predictions.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above the round's average — it names three queries, reports IDs rather than impressions, states the channel, and correctly identifies 2608.12218 as the mechanism source instead of hiding it — but it is over-narrow in a way that inflates its own verdict: all three queries are long conjunctive strings, Q1 returned literally one hit, and a single-hit query is evidence about the query, not about the field. It searched only the agent/distillation side and never the RAG side, where the same manipulation lives. My queries, all via the s2cli literature command (WebSearch unavailable this session; WebFetch never used): (Q1, --recent, answered by hf) 'training-time context dose ... reduces parametric encoding memory-free evaluation' -> 2608.12218 top hit, then off-topic (2605.09932 FocuSFT, 2605.28819 PEFT-Arena); (Q2, unrestricted, hf) 'retrieval-augmented fine-tuning number of retrieved documents distractors during training affects reliance on context' -> 2608.12218 again, plus 2410.05983 (degradation as retrieved passages increase, with training-based robustness fixes) and 2310.01558 (fine-tuning on mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts to change reliance) — the dose axis and the decoy idea in QA, absent from the proposal's related work; (Q3, --recent, hf) agent-side dose/crutch query -> 2605.05413 (From History to State: moving procedural context from prompts to weights), 2606.04536, 2606.03197; nothing with a k_train ladder; (Q4, --recent, hf) 'training with memory in the prompt makes the memory-free policy worse ... dose of in-context examples' -> 2606.01967 (Training Prompt Matters: training prompts shape learning dynamics, prompts identifiable by task-loss analysis), 2606.04703 (continual experience internalization: granularity, injection patterns, internalization regimes), 2510.05024 (Inoculation Prompting: train-time prompt content controls what is learned) — three papers in the proposal's own conceptual family that its check did not surface; (Q5, --recent, hf) Pareto/no-dominant-checkpoint query -> 2607.21051 (Experience Distillation), 2605.10889, 2605.27140; nothing claiming a dose-dependent Pareto front. arXiv IDs VERIFIED by `s2cli paper` (s2 channel): 2608.12218, 2603.18272, 2606.29502 (UCOB), 2509.16189 (latent learning, TMLR), 2607.28272 (MemHarness), 2607.01480 (PMD, memory-free at inference). NOT verified, cited in the related work and left unchecked: 2602.12275 (OPCD), 2601.18734 (OPSD), 2604.10674 (Skill-SD), 2608.13040, 2608.01735 (DAPD), 2606.30626 (DOPD), 2608.09228 (OP2SD), 2607.10608, 2604.04949, 2603.27813, 2603.10600 — none is load-bearing for the novelty argument, so I did not spend the shared rate limit on them, but the two that would change my score if checked are 2603.18272's ablation section (does retrieval-aware fine-tuning already sweep k?) and 2606.04703's 'injection patterns' finding; neither is verifiable without section text, and the proposal did not try.
